points.title: 是 to be
points.meaning: Links two nouns: "A is B".
explain: 是 joins a subject to a noun: who or what something is. Negate it with 不是.
是 isn't used before adjectives: say 我很忙, not 我是忙.

examples.py: Wǒ shì xuéshēng.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄕˋ ㄒㄩㄝˊ ㄕㄥ。
examples.en: I'm a student.

examples.py: Tā bù shì lǎoshī, tā shì yīshēng.
examples.zy: ㄊㄚ ㄅㄨˋ ㄕˋ ㄌㄠˇ ㄕ， ㄊㄚ ㄕˋ ㄧ ㄕㄥ。
examples.en: He isn't a teacher; he's a doctor.

examples.py: Zhè shì wǒ de shǒujī.
examples.zy: ㄓㄜˋ ㄕˋ ㄨㄛˇ ˙ㄉㄜ ㄕㄡˇ ㄐㄧ。
examples.en: This is my phone.

points.title: 嗎 yes/no questions
points.meaning: Turns a statement into a yes/no question.
explain: Add 嗎 to the end of a statement; the word order stays the same. To answer "yes", repeat the verb (是, 有, 要). To answer "no", negate it (不是, 沒有, 不要).

examples.py: Nǐ shì Táiwān rén ma?
examples.zy: ㄋㄧˇ ㄕˋ ㄊㄞˊ ㄨㄢ ㄖㄣˊ ˙ㄇㄚ？
examples.en: Are you Taiwanese?

examples.py: Nǐ xǐhuān hē kāfēi ma?
examples.zy: ㄋㄧˇ ㄒㄧˇ ㄏㄨㄢ ㄏㄜ ㄎㄚ ㄈㄟ ˙ㄇㄚ？
examples.en: Do you like coffee?

examples.py: Nǐ yǒu shíjiān ma?
examples.zy: ㄋㄧˇ ㄧㄡˇ ㄕˊ ㄐㄧㄢ ˙ㄇㄚ？
examples.en: Do you have time?

points.title: 很 + adjective
points.meaning: Describes something with an adjective. No 是 needed.
explain: Chinese adjectives work like verbs, so they don't take 是. A bare adjective sounds like a contrast ("this one's big, that one isn't"), so 很 is usually added. Here 很 is unstressed and hardly means "very".

examples.py: Jīntiān hěn rè.
examples.zy: ㄐㄧㄣ ㄊㄧㄢ ㄏㄣˇ ㄖㄜˋ。
examples.en: It's hot today.

examples.zh: 這家店的牛肉麵很好吃。
examples.py: Zhè jiā diàn de niúròu miàn hěn hǎochī.
examples.zy: ㄓㄜˋ ㄐㄧㄚ ㄉㄧㄢˋ ˙ㄉㄜ ㄋㄧㄡˊ ㄖㄡˋ ㄇㄧㄢˋ ㄏㄣˇ ㄏㄠˇ ㄔ。
examples.en: This shop's beef noodles are delicious.

examples.py: Wǒ zuìjìn hěn máng.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄗㄨㄟˋ ㄐㄧㄣˋ ㄏㄣˇ ㄇㄤˊ。
examples.en: I've been busy lately.

notes: In speech, 很 is often swapped for 好 or 超: 好熱喔！ 超好吃！

points.title: 不 and 沒 negation
points.meaning: 不 for habits, wishes, the present and the future. 沒(有) for what didn't happen.
explain: 不 negates what you do, want or are: 我不喝酒 "I don't drink". 沒 or 沒有 says something didn't or hasn't happened: 我沒喝 "I didn't drink it".
有 is always negated with 沒: 沒有, never 不有.

examples.py: Wǒ bù chī ròu.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄅㄨˋ ㄔ ㄖㄡˋ。
examples.en: I don't eat meat.

examples.py: Tā zuótiān méi lái shàngkè.
examples.zy: ㄊㄚ ㄗㄨㄛˊ ㄊㄧㄢ ㄇㄟˊ ㄌㄞˊ ㄕㄤˋ ㄎㄜˋ。
examples.en: He didn't come to class yesterday.

examples.py: Wǒ méiyǒu qián.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄇㄟˊ ㄧㄡˇ ㄑㄧㄢˊ。
examples.en: I don't have any money.

points.title: 有 have, there is
points.meaning: "To have", and also "there is / there are".
explain: With a person as the subject, 有 means "have". With a place as the subject, it means "there is". The negative is 沒有.

examples.py: Wǒ yǒu yī ge gēge.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄧㄡˇ ㄧ ˙ㄍㄜ ㄍㄜ ˙ㄍㄜ。
examples.en: I have an older brother.

examples.py: Fùjìn yǒu biànlì shāngdiàn ma?
examples.zy: ㄈㄨˋ ㄐㄧㄣˋ ㄧㄡˇ ㄅㄧㄢˋ ㄌㄧˋ ㄕㄤ ㄉㄧㄢˋ ˙ㄇㄚ？
examples.en: Is there a convenience store nearby?

examples.py: Bīngxiāng lǐ méiyǒu niúnǎi le.
examples.zy: ㄅㄧㄥ ㄒㄧㄤ ㄌㄧˇ ㄇㄟˊ ㄧㄡˇ ㄋㄧㄡˊ ㄋㄞˇ ˙ㄌㄜ。
examples.en: There's no milk left in the fridge.

points.title: 的 possession
points.meaning: "A's B": links an owner or a description to a noun.
explain: 的 works like English 's: 老師的書 "the teacher's book". It also links a description to a noun: 新的手機 "a new phone".
With close family and groups you belong to, 的 is usually dropped: 我媽媽, 我們學校.

examples.py: Zhè shì shéi de yǔsǎn?
examples.zy: ㄓㄜˋ ㄕˋ ㄕㄟˊ ˙ㄉㄜ ㄩˇ ㄙㄢˇ？
examples.en: Whose umbrella is this?

examples.py: Wǒ māma shì lǎoshī.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄇㄚ ˙ㄇㄚ ㄕˋ ㄌㄠˇ ㄕ。
examples.en: My mom is a teacher.

examples.zh: 我想買一件紅色的外套。
examples.py: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yī jiàn hóngsè de wàitào.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄒㄧㄤˇ ㄇㄞˇ ㄧ ㄐㄧㄢˋ ㄏㄨㄥˊ ㄙㄜˋ ˙ㄉㄜ ㄨㄞˋ ㄊㄠˋ。
examples.en: I want to buy a red jacket.

points.title: Question words stay in place
points.pattern: 什麼 · 誰 · 哪裡 · 幾 · 多少
points.meaning: Question words go where the answer would go.
explain: English moves question words to the front; Chinese leaves them where the answer goes. Don't add 嗎 to these questions.
幾 asks about small numbers (usually under 10) and needs a measure word. 多少 is for any amount.

examples.py: Nǐ jiào shénme míngzi?
examples.zy: ㄋㄧˇ ㄐㄧㄠˋ ㄕㄣˊ ˙ㄇㄜ ㄇㄧㄥˊ ˙ㄗ？
examples.en: What's your name?

examples.py: Nǐ zhù zài nǎlǐ?
examples.zy: ㄋㄧˇ ㄓㄨˋ ㄗㄞˋ ㄋㄚˇ ㄌㄧˇ？
examples.en: Where do you live?

examples.py: Zhè ge duōshǎo qián?
examples.zy: ㄓㄜˋ ˙ㄍㄜ ㄉㄨㄛ ㄕㄠˇ ㄑㄧㄢˊ？
examples.en: How much is this?

examples.py: Nǐ yǒu jǐ ge xiōngdì jiěmèi?
examples.zy: ㄋㄧˇ ㄧㄡˇ ㄐㄧˇ ˙ㄍㄜ ㄒㄩㄥ ㄉㄧˋ ㄐㄧㄝˇ ㄇㄟˋ？
examples.en: How many brothers and sisters do you have?

notes: 哪裡 is the usual word for "where" in Taiwan. 哪兒 sounds northern. 姊妹 is the Taiwan spelling (mainland 姐妹).

points.title: 呢 "and…?"
points.meaning: Asks the same question about someone else, or "where is…?".
explain: After answering, 你呢？ turns the question back: "And you?". On its own, 我的手機呢？ means "Where's my phone?".

examples.py: Wǒ hěn hǎo, nǐ ne?
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄏㄣˇ ㄏㄠˇ， ㄋㄧˇ ˙ㄋㄜ？
examples.en: I'm fine. And you?

examples.py: Wǒ yào hē hóngchá, nǐ ne?
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄧㄠˋ ㄏㄜ ㄏㄨㄥˊ ㄔㄚˊ， ㄋㄧˇ ˙ㄋㄜ？
examples.en: I'll have black tea. What about you?

examples.py: Wǒ de yàoshi ne?
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ˙ㄉㄜ ㄧㄠˋ ˙ㄕ ˙ㄋㄜ？
examples.en: Where are my keys?

points.title: A-not-A questions
points.pattern: V 不 V？ · 有沒有？
points.meaning: 好不好, 是不是, 有沒有: asks yes or no by giving both options.
explain: Saying a verb or adjective and then its negative makes a yes/no question, like 嗎. Don't add 嗎 as well. For 有 it's 有沒有.
Two-syllable words often shorten: 喜不喜歡.

examples.py: Nǐ míngtiān yǒu méiyǒu kòng?
examples.zy: ㄋㄧˇ ㄇㄧㄥˊ ㄊㄧㄢ ㄧㄡˇ ㄇㄟˊ ㄧㄡˇ ㄎㄨㄥˋ？
examples.en: Are you free tomorrow?

examples.py: Zhè ge hǎo bù hǎochī?
examples.zy: ㄓㄜˋ ˙ㄍㄜ ㄏㄠˇ ㄅㄨˋ ㄏㄠˇ ㄔ？
examples.en: Is this tasty?

examples.py: Nǐ xǐ bù xǐhuān Táiběi?
examples.zy: ㄋㄧˇ ㄒㄧˇ ㄅㄨˋ ㄒㄧˇ ㄏㄨㄢ ㄊㄞˊ ㄅㄟˇ？
examples.en: Do you like Taipei?

notes: 有沒有 + verb is very common for past events: 你有沒有吃早餐？ "Did you have breakfast?"

points.title: Basic word order
points.meaning: Time and place come before the verb.
explain: The usual order is subject, time, place, then the verb and its object. The time can also go before the subject.

examples.py: Wǒ míngtiān zài jiā gōngzuò.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄇㄧㄥˊ ㄊㄧㄢ ㄗㄞˋ ㄐㄧㄚ ㄍㄨㄥ ㄗㄨㄛˋ。
examples.en: I'm working from home tomorrow.

examples.zh: 我們晚上七點在捷運站見面。
examples.py: Wǒmen wǎnshàng qī diǎn zài jiéyùn zhàn jiànmiàn.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ˙ㄇㄣ ㄨㄢˇ ㄕㄤˋ ㄑㄧ ㄉㄧㄢˇ ㄗㄞˋ ㄐㄧㄝˊ ㄩㄣˋ ㄓㄢˋ ㄐㄧㄢˋ ㄇㄧㄢˋ。
examples.en: Let's meet at the MRT station at seven tonight.

examples.py: Xià ge xīngqí wǒ yào qù Táinán.
examples.zy: ㄒㄧㄚˋ ˙ㄍㄜ ㄒㄧㄥ ㄑㄧˊ ㄨㄛˇ ㄧㄠˋ ㄑㄩˋ ㄊㄞˊ ㄋㄢˊ。
examples.en: Next week I'm going to Tainan.

points.title: 在 at, in
points.meaning: "To be at" a place, or where an action happens.
explain: On its own, 在 + place means "is at": 他在家. Before another verb it says where the action happens: 在家吃飯.
The place doesn't go after the verb, except with a few verbs such as 住在 and 放在.

examples.py: Lǎoshī zài jiàoshì.
examples.zy: ㄌㄠˇ ㄕ ㄗㄞˋ ㄐㄧㄠˋ ㄕˋ。
examples.en: The teacher is in the classroom.

examples.py: Wǒ zài chāoshāng mǎi zǎocān.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄗㄞˋ ㄔㄠ ㄕㄤ ㄇㄞˇ ㄗㄠˇ ㄘㄢ。
examples.en: I buy breakfast at the convenience store.

examples.py: Tā zhù zài Xīnzhú.
examples.zy: ㄊㄚ ㄓㄨˋ ㄗㄞˋ ㄒㄧㄣ ㄓㄨˊ。
examples.en: He lives in Hsinchu.

notes: 超商 (short for 便利商店) is what most people call 7-Eleven or FamilyMart.

points.title: 也 and 都
points.meaning: 也 "also" and 都 "all, both" go right before the verb.
explain: Unlike English "also", 也 can't start a sentence or come after the verb. 都 refers back to a plural subject: 我們都是學生 "We're all students". Together they're 也都.
A question word + 都 means "every…" or, with a negative, "no…": 什麼都不吃 "won't eat anything".

examples.py: Wǒ yě shì xuéshēng.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄧㄝˇ ㄕˋ ㄒㄩㄝˊ ㄕㄥ。
examples.en: I'm a student too.

examples.py: Wǒmen dōu xǐhuān chī là.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ˙ㄇㄣ ㄉㄡ ㄒㄧˇ ㄏㄨㄢ ㄔ ㄌㄚˋ。
examples.en: We all like spicy food.

examples.py: Tā shénme dōu bù chī.
examples.zy: ㄊㄚ ㄕㄣˊ ˙ㄇㄜ ㄉㄡ ㄅㄨˋ ㄔ。
examples.en: He won't eat anything.

points.title: 想 and 要 want
points.meaning: 想 "would like to". 要 "want to, going to".
explain: 想 is softer: a wish. 要 is firmer: a decision or a plan. In shops 要 means "I'll have".
不想 is "don't want to". 不要 usually means "don't!".

examples.py: Wǒ xiǎng qù Rìběn wán.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄒㄧㄤˇ ㄑㄩˋ ㄖˋ ㄅㄣˇ ㄨㄢˊ。
examples.en: I'd like to go to Japan on holiday.

examples.py: Wǒ yào yī bēi rè kāfēi.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄧㄠˋ ㄧ ㄅㄟ ㄖㄜˋ ㄎㄚ ㄈㄟ。
examples.en: I'll have a hot coffee.

examples.py: Bù yào pèng! Hěn tàng.
examples.zy: ㄅㄨˋ ㄧㄠˋ ㄆㄥˋ！ ㄏㄣˇ ㄊㄤˋ。
examples.en: Don't touch! It's hot.

points.title: 會, 能, 可以 can
points.pattern: 會 / 能 / 可以 + Verb
points.meaning: 會 for skills and likelihood, 能 for ability, 可以 for permission.
explain: 會 is "know how to" (會游泳) and also "will, is likely to" (明天會下雨). 能 is being able to in the situation (我今天不能喝酒: I'm driving). 可以 asks for or gives permission. 能 and 可以 often overlap.

examples.py: Nǐ huì shuō Zhōngwén ma?
examples.zy: ㄋㄧˇ ㄏㄨㄟˋ ㄕㄨㄛ ㄓㄨㄥ ㄨㄣˊ ˙ㄇㄚ？
examples.en: Can you speak Chinese?

examples.py: Míngtiān huì xiàyǔ.
examples.zy: ㄇㄧㄥˊ ㄊㄧㄢ ㄏㄨㄟˋ ㄒㄧㄚˋ ㄩˇ。
examples.en: It's going to rain tomorrow.

examples.zh: 我今天要開車，不能喝酒。
examples.py: Wǒ jīntiān yào kāichē, bù néng hē jiǔ.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄐㄧㄣ ㄊㄧㄢ ㄧㄠˋ ㄎㄞ ㄔㄜ， ㄅㄨˋ ㄋㄥˊ ㄏㄜ ㄐㄧㄡˇ。
examples.en: I'm driving today, so I can't drink.

examples.py: Zhèlǐ kěyǐ pāizhào ma?
examples.zy: ㄓㄜˋ ㄌㄧˇ ㄎㄜˇ ㄧˇ ㄆㄞ ㄓㄠˋ ˙ㄇㄚ？
examples.en: Can I take photos here?

notes: 不會 is also the polite reply to 謝謝 ("not at all"). 會不會 + adjective softens a question: 會不會太貴？ "Isn't it a bit expensive?"

points.title: Verb + 了 completed
points.meaning: Marks an action as done.
explain: 了 after a verb says the action is complete. It isn't a past tense: past habits don't take it. The negative is 沒(有) + verb, without 了.
With a simple object, the sentence usually needs more after it, such as a number: 我買了兩本書.

examples.py: Wǒ mǎi le liǎng zhāng diànyǐng piào.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄇㄞˇ ˙ㄌㄜ ㄌㄧㄤˇ ㄓㄤ ㄉㄧㄢˋ ㄧㄥˇ ㄆㄧㄠˋ。
examples.en: I bought two movie tickets.

examples.zh: 他吃了早餐就去上班了。
examples.py: Tā chī le zǎocān jiù qù shàngbān le.
examples.zy: ㄊㄚ ㄔ ˙ㄌㄜ ㄗㄠˇ ㄘㄢ ㄐㄧㄡˋ ㄑㄩˋ ㄕㄤˋ ㄅㄢ ˙ㄌㄜ。
examples.en: He had breakfast and then went to work.

examples.py: Wǒ hái méi chī wǔcān.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄏㄞˊ ㄇㄟˊ ㄔ ㄨˇ ㄘㄢ。
examples.en: I haven't had lunch yet.

points.title: Sentence + 了 new situation
points.meaning: At the end of a sentence, 了 says something has changed.
explain: Final 了 marks a new state: 下雨了 "It's started raining", 我餓了 "I'm hungry now". With 不 it means "not anymore": 我不去了 "I'm not going after all".

examples.py: Xiàyǔ le!
examples.zy: ㄒㄧㄚˋ ㄩˇ ˙ㄌㄜ！
examples.en: It's raining!

examples.py: Wǒ èrshíwǔ suì le.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄦˋ ㄕˊ ㄨˇ ㄙㄨㄟˋ ˙ㄌㄜ。
examples.en: I'm 25 now.

examples.py: Tài wǎn le, wǒ bù qù le.
examples.zy: ㄊㄞˋ ㄨㄢˇ ˙ㄌㄜ， ㄨㄛˇ ㄅㄨˋ ㄑㄩˋ ˙ㄌㄜ。
examples.en: It's too late. I'm not going after all.

points.title: Verb + 過 experience
points.meaning: "Have (ever) done": an experience at some point.
explain: 過 after a verb says you've had the experience. The negative is 沒(有) + V + 過, and 從來沒 is "never".

examples.py: Wǒ qù guò Huālián.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄑㄩˋ ㄍㄨㄛˋ ㄏㄨㄚ ㄌㄧㄢˊ。
examples.en: I've been to Hualien.

examples.py: Nǐ chī guò chòu dòufu ma?
examples.zy: ㄋㄧˇ ㄔ ㄍㄨㄛˋ ㄔㄡˋ ㄉㄡˋ ˙ㄈㄨ ˙ㄇㄚ？
examples.en: Have you ever tried stinky tofu?

examples.py: Wǒ cónglái méi kàn guò xuě.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄘㄨㄥˊ ㄌㄞˊ ㄇㄟˊ ㄎㄢˋ ㄍㄨㄛˋ ㄒㄩㄝˇ。
examples.en: I've never seen snow.

notes: In Taiwan you'll often hear 有 + V + 過: 你有去過墾丁嗎？

points.title: 有 + Verb (Taiwan)
points.meaning: Taiwan Mandarin uses 有 to say that something did happen.
explain: In Taiwan, 有 before a verb confirms that an action happened, like a stressed English "did". It's the natural partner of 沒有 + V. Mainland speakers mostly avoid it, but in Taiwan it's everyday speech.

examples.zh: 我有打電話給你，你沒接。
examples.py: Wǒ yǒu dǎ diànhuà gěi nǐ, nǐ méi jiē.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄧㄡˇ ㄉㄚˇ ㄉㄧㄢˋ ㄏㄨㄚˋ ㄍㄟˇ ㄋㄧˇ， ㄋㄧˇ ㄇㄟˊ ㄐㄧㄝ。
examples.en: I did call you. You didn't pick up.

examples.py: Nǐ jīntiān yǒu yùndòng ma?
examples.zy: ㄋㄧˇ ㄐㄧㄣ ㄊㄧㄢ ㄧㄡˇ ㄩㄣˋ ㄉㄨㄥˋ ˙ㄇㄚ？
examples.en: Did you exercise today?

examples.py: Wǒ yǒu kàn dào nǐ de xùnxí.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄧㄡˇ ㄎㄢˋ ㄉㄠˋ ㄋㄧˇ ˙ㄉㄜ ㄒㄩㄣˋ ㄒㄧˊ。
examples.en: I saw your message.

points.title: 在 + Verb in progress
points.meaning: "Is doing (right now)".
explain: 在 before a verb says the action is going on. 正在 stresses "right this moment".

examples.py: Tā zài xǐzǎo.
examples.zy: ㄊㄚ ㄗㄞˋ ㄒㄧˇ ㄗㄠˇ。
examples.en: He's in the shower.

examples.py: Nǐ zài zuò shénme?
examples.zy: ㄋㄧˇ ㄗㄞˋ ㄗㄨㄛˋ ㄕㄣˊ ˙ㄇㄜ？
examples.en: What are you doing?

examples.py: Wǒmen zài děng gōngchē.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ˙ㄇㄣ ㄗㄞˋ ㄉㄥˇ ㄍㄨㄥ ㄔㄜ。

points.title: 吧 suggestions
points.meaning: "Let's…", "…, right?": softens a suggestion or checks a guess.
explain: After a suggestion, 吧 means "let's" or "how about". After a statement it means "I suppose…?", asking the listener to agree.

examples.py: Wǒmen zǒu ba!

points.title: 太…了 too, so
points.meaning: "Too…", or for good things "so…!".
explain: 太…了 is "too" for problems (太貴了) and an exclamation for good things (太好了！). 不太 + adjective is a soft "not very".

examples.en: That's too expensive. Could you make it a bit cheaper?

examples.py: Tài hǎo le!
examples.zy: ㄊㄞˋ ㄏㄠˇ ˙ㄌㄜ！
examples.en: Great!

examples.py: Wǒ bù tài shūfu.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄅㄨˋ ㄊㄞˋ ㄕㄨ ˙ㄈㄨ。
examples.en: I'm not feeling very well.

points.title: Verb + 一下 briefly
points.meaning: Makes a request softer: "just…", "for a moment".
explain: 一下 after a verb means doing it briefly. It makes requests polite: 等一下 "wait a moment", 請你看一下 "please take a look".

examples.py: Qǐng děng yīxià.

examples.en: Can I borrow your pen for a sec?

examples.py: Wǒmen xiūxí yīxià ba.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ˙ㄇㄣ ㄒㄧㄡ ㄒㄧˊ ㄧ ㄒㄧㄚˋ ˙ㄅㄚ。
examples.en: Let's take a short break.

points.title: 跟…一起 with
points.meaning: "Do something (together) with someone".
explain: 跟 + person goes before the verb. 一起 "together" is often added.

examples.zh: 我週末跟朋友一起去爬山。
examples.py: Wǒ zhōumò gēn péngyǒu yīqǐ qù páshān.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄓㄡ ㄇㄛˋ ㄍㄣ ㄆㄥˊ ㄧㄡˇ ㄧ ㄑㄧˇ ㄑㄩˋ ㄆㄚˊ ㄕㄢ。

examples.en: Do you want to eat with us?

examples.py: Wǒ gēn tā bù shóu.

examples.en: I don't know him well.

notes: In Taiwan speech, 跟 is far more common than 和 for "and" and "with".

points.title: 比 comparisons
points.meaning: "A is more … than B".
explain: Put 比 + B before the adjective. 很 can't be used here, but 更 "even more" can, and the size of the difference goes after the adjective: 他比我高十公分 "He's 10 cm taller than me". 多了 is "much more".

examples.py: Táiběi bǐ Táinán lěng.

examples.en: He's two years older than me.

points.title: 沒有…那麼 not as
points.pattern: A 沒有 B (那麼) + Adj
points.meaning: "A isn't as … as B".
explain: The negative of a 比 comparison is usually 沒有, not 不比. 那麼 or 這麼 "that, so" is often added.

examples.py: Jīntiān méiyǒu zuótiān nàme rè.
examples.zy: ㄐㄧㄣ ㄊㄧㄢ ㄇㄟˊ ㄧㄡˇ ㄗㄨㄛˊ ㄊㄧㄢ ㄋㄚˋ ˙ㄇㄜ ㄖㄜˋ。
examples.en: Today isn't as hot as yesterday.

examples.py: Wǒ de Zhōngwén méiyǒu nǐ hǎo.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ˙ㄉㄜ ㄓㄨㄥ ㄨㄣˊ ㄇㄟˊ ㄧㄡˇ ㄋㄧˇ ㄏㄠˇ。
examples.en: My Chinese isn't as good as yours.

examples.en: This place isn't as expensive as that one.

points.title: 跟…一樣 the same as
points.pattern: A 跟 B 一樣 (+ Adj)
points.meaning: "A is the same as B", "as … as".
explain: 一樣 "the same" can stand alone or come before an adjective: 跟他一樣高 "as tall as him". The negative is 不一樣.

examples.py: Wǒ de shǒujī gēn nǐ de yīyàng.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ˙ㄉㄜ ㄕㄡˇ ㄐㄧ ㄍㄣ ㄋㄧˇ ˙ㄉㄜ ㄧ ㄧㄤˋ。
examples.en: My phone is the same as yours.

examples.py: Tā gēn tā bàba yīyàng gāo.
examples.zy: ㄊㄚ ㄍㄣ ㄊㄚ ㄅㄚˋ ˙ㄅㄚ ㄧ ㄧㄤˋ ㄍㄠ。
examples.en: He's as tall as his dad.

examples.zh: 台灣的中文跟大陸的不太一樣。
examples.py: Táiwān de Zhōngwén gēn dàlù de bù tài yīyàng.
examples.zy: ㄊㄞˊ ㄨㄢ ˙ㄉㄜ ㄓㄨㄥ ㄨㄣˊ ㄍㄣ ㄉㄚˋ ㄌㄨˋ ˙ㄉㄜ ㄅㄨˋ ㄊㄞˋ ㄧ ㄧㄤˋ。
examples.en: Taiwan's Chinese is a bit different from the mainland's.

points.title: Verb + 得 + description
points.meaning: Says how something is done: well, fast, badly.
explain: 得 after a verb introduces a description of how it's done: 說得很好 "speaks well". With an object, repeat the verb (他說中文說得很好) or put the object first (他中文說得很好).

examples.py: Nǐ Zhōngwén shuō de hěn hǎo!
examples.zy: ㄋㄧˇ ㄓㄨㄥ ㄨㄣˊ ㄕㄨㄛ ˙ㄉㄜ ㄏㄣˇ ㄏㄠˇ！
examples.en: Your Chinese is very good!

examples.py: Tā pǎo de hěn kuài.

examples.en: He runs fast.

examples.py: Wǒ zuótiān shuì de bù hǎo.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄗㄨㄛˊ ㄊㄧㄢ ㄕㄨㄟˋ ˙ㄉㄜ ㄅㄨˋ ㄏㄠˇ。
examples.en: I didn't sleep well last night.

notes: The modest reply to a compliment is 哪裡哪裡 or 還好啦, rather than 謝謝.

points.title: 的 descriptions before nouns
points.meaning: "The … that …": a whole clause can describe a noun.
explain: Anything describing a noun, even a full clause, goes before it with 的: 我昨天買的書 "the book I bought yesterday". The noun can be left out when it's clear: 我買的 "the one I bought".

examples.zh: 我昨天買的衣服太小了。
examples.py: Wǒ zuótiān mǎi de yīfú tài xiǎo le.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄗㄨㄛˊ ㄊㄧㄢ ㄇㄞˇ ˙ㄉㄜ ㄧ ㄈㄨˊ ㄊㄞˋ ㄒㄧㄠˇ ˙ㄌㄜ。

examples.py: Nǐ shuō de nà jiā diàn zài nǎlǐ?

examples.en: Where's the shop you mentioned?

points.title: 因為…所以 because … so
points.meaning: "Because A, (so) B".
explain: English uses either "because" or "so"; Chinese often uses both. Either one can be left out. The reason usually comes first.

examples.zh: 因為下雨，所以我們不去了。

examples.zh: 我今天很累，因為昨天加班。

examples.en: I'm tired today because I worked late yesterday.

examples.py: Tā gǎnmào le, suǒyǐ méi lái.
examples.zy: ㄊㄚ ㄍㄢˇ ㄇㄠˋ ˙ㄌㄜ， ㄙㄨㄛˇ ㄧˇ ㄇㄟˊ ㄌㄞˊ。

points.title: 雖然…但是 although
points.pattern: 雖然 A，但是 / 可是 B
points.meaning: "Although A, B".
explain: Chinese keeps both halves: 雖然…但是 (or 可是). 雖然 can come before or after the subject.

examples.zy: ㄊㄚ ㄙㄨㄟ ㄖㄢˊ ㄏㄣˇ ㄇㄤˊ， ㄎㄜˇ ㄕˋ ㄇㄟˇ ㄊㄧㄢ ㄉㄡ ㄩㄣˋ ㄉㄨㄥˋ。
examples.en: Although he's busy, he exercises every day.

examples.zh: 雖然我學了三年中文，但是還聽不懂台語。
examples.py: Suīrán wǒ xué le sān nián Zhōngwén, dànshì hái tīng bù dǒng Táiyǔ.
examples.zy: ㄙㄨㄟ ㄖㄢˊ ㄨㄛˇ ㄒㄩㄝˊ ˙ㄌㄜ ㄙㄢ ㄋㄧㄢˊ ㄓㄨㄥ ㄨㄣˊ， ㄉㄢˋ ㄕˋ ㄏㄞˊ ㄊㄧㄥ ㄅㄨˋ ㄉㄨㄥˇ ㄊㄞˊ ㄩˇ。
examples.en: I've studied Chinese for three years, but I still can't understand Taiwanese.

points.title: 快要…了 about to
points.meaning: "Is about to…", "soon".
explain: 快要…了, 要…了 and 快…了 all say something will happen very soon. With a clock time, use 要…了, not 快要: 火車十點就要開了.

examples.py: Kuài yào xiàyǔ le.
examples.zy: ㄎㄨㄞˋ ㄧㄠˋ ㄒㄧㄚˋ ㄩˇ ˙ㄌㄜ。
examples.en: It's about to rain.

examples.py: Diànyǐng yào kāishǐ le.
examples.zy: ㄉㄧㄢˋ ㄧㄥˇ ㄧㄠˋ ㄎㄞ ㄕˇ ˙ㄌㄜ。
examples.en: The movie's about to start.

examples.py: Wǒ kuài sānshí suì le.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄎㄨㄞˋ ㄙㄢ ㄕˊ ㄙㄨㄟˋ ˙ㄌㄜ。
examples.en: I'm almost 30.

points.title: 已經…了 already
points.meaning: "Already".
explain: 已經 goes before the verb, usually with 了 at the end.

examples.py: Wǒ yǐjīng chībǎo le.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄧˇ ㄐㄧㄥ ㄔ ㄅㄠˇ ˙ㄌㄜ。
examples.en: I'm already full.

examples.py: Tā yǐjīng dào le.
examples.zy: ㄊㄚ ㄧˇ ㄐㄧㄥ ㄉㄠˋ ˙ㄌㄜ。
examples.en: He's already here.

examples.zh: 已經十二點了，快去睡覺！
examples.py: Yǐjīng shí èr diǎn le, kuài qù shuìjiào!
examples.zy: ㄧˇ ㄐㄧㄥ ㄕˊ ㄦˋ ㄉㄧㄢˇ ˙ㄌㄜ， ㄎㄨㄞˋ ㄑㄩˋ ㄕㄨㄟˋ ㄐㄧㄠˋ！

points.title: 才 and 就 late or early
points.meaning: 就 "already, as early as". 才 "not until".
explain: After a time, 就 says it happened earlier or faster than expected and usually takes 了. 才 says it was later than expected and doesn't take 了.

examples.py: Wǒ qī diǎn jiù dào le.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄑㄧ ㄉㄧㄢˇ ㄐㄧㄡˋ ㄉㄠˋ ˙ㄌㄜ。
examples.en: I got there at seven already.

examples.py: Tā shí diǎn cái qǐchuáng.
examples.zy: ㄊㄚ ㄕˊ ㄉㄧㄢˇ ㄘㄞˊ ㄑㄧˇ ㄔㄨㄤˊ。

examples.py: Wǒ zuótiān bànyè cái huíjiā.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄗㄨㄛˊ ㄊㄧㄢ ㄅㄢˋ ㄧㄝˋ ㄘㄞˊ ㄏㄨㄟˊ ㄐㄧㄚ。

points.title: 把 sentences
points.meaning: Puts the object before the verb to say what was done to it.
explain: 把 moves the object in front of the verb. It's used for handling or moving things: putting, finishing, taking away. The verb can't stand alone; it needs a result such as 完, 好, 上, 到 + place, 給 + person, or 了.

examples.py: Qǐng bǎ mén guān shàng.

examples.py: Wǒ bǎ zuòyè xiě wán le.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ㄅㄚˇ ㄗㄨㄛˋ ㄧㄝˋ ㄒㄧㄝˇ ㄨㄢˊ ˙ㄌㄜ。
examples.en: I've finished my homework.

examples.py: Nǐ bǎ shǒujī fàng zài nǎlǐ le?
examples.zy: ㄋㄧˇ ㄅㄚˇ ㄕㄡˇ ㄐㄧ ㄈㄤˋ ㄗㄞˋ ㄋㄚˇ ㄌㄧˇ ˙ㄌㄜ？

points.title: 被 passive
points.meaning: "Was …ed (by)": mostly for something unwelcome.
explain: 被 makes the thing affected the subject. The doer can follow 被 or be left out. Like 把, the verb needs a result. It's mostly used for bad news.

examples.py: Wǒ de jiǎotàchē bèi tōu le.
examples.zy: ㄨㄛˇ ˙ㄉㄜ ㄐㄧㄠˇ ㄊㄚˋ ㄔㄜ ㄅㄟˋ ㄊㄡ ˙ㄌㄜ。
examples.en: My bike was stolen.

examples.py: Tā bèi lǎobǎn mà le.
examples.zy: ㄊㄚ ㄅㄟˋ ㄌㄠˇ ㄅㄢˇ ㄇㄚˋ ˙ㄌㄜ。

examples.py: Dàngāo bèi dìdi chī wán le.
examples.zy: ㄉㄤˋ ㄠ ㄅㄟˋ ㄉㄧˋ ˙ㄉㄧ ㄔ ㄨㄢˊ ˙ㄌㄜ。
examples.en: My little brother ate all the cake.

notes: In speech, 給 often replaces 被: 我的錢包給人偷了.

points.title: 讓 and 叫 let, make, tell
points.pattern: A 讓 / 叫 B + V
points.meaning: "A lets / makes / tells B do something".
explain: 讓 is "let" or "make (someone feel)": 讓我想一下 "let me think". 叫 is "tell someone to": 媽媽叫我回家.

examples.py: Ràng wǒ xiǎng yī xiǎng.
examples.zy: ㄖㄤˋ ㄨㄛˇ ㄒㄧㄤˇ ㄧ ㄒㄧㄤˇ。
examples.en: Let me think about it.

examples.zh: 老闆叫我明天早一點來。
examples.py: Lǎobǎn jiào wǒ míngtiān zǎo yīdiǎn lái.
examples.zy: ㄌㄠˇ ㄅㄢˇ ㄐㄧㄠˋ ㄨㄛˇ ㄇㄧㄥˊ ㄊㄧㄢ ㄗㄠˇ ㄧ ㄉㄧㄢˇ ㄌㄞˊ。
examples.en: My boss told me to come in a bit earlier tomorrow.

examples.zh: 這個消息讓大家很開心。
examples.py: Zhè ge xiāoxí ràng dàjiā hěn kāixīn.
examples.zy: ㄓㄜˋ ˙ㄍㄜ ㄒㄧㄠ ㄒㄧˊ ㄖㄤˋ ㄉㄚˋ ㄐㄧㄚ ㄏㄣˇ ㄎㄞ ㄒㄧㄣ。
examples.en: The news made everyone happy.

points.title: How long
points.meaning: "For two hours", "for three years": the length of time goes after the verb.
explain: The length of time goes after the verb. With an object, repeat the verb (學中文學了兩年) or put the time before the object (學了兩年中文).
